target_customer: US government defense buyers and prime contractors that need aerospace parts
problem: Defense parts are slow and expensive to source and manufacture; small suppliers struggle to win contracts and the government waits long for delivery.
business_model: Acts as a defense prime: wins government contracts and fulfills them through automated manufacturing and a supplier network
product_category: AI-native defense manufacturing and supply chain

founders.name: Kaya Celebi
education: Duke University, BSc computer science and statistics
founders.background_notes: YC page says ML engineer at Morgan Stanley and AI tech lead at Hartree Partners.

founders.name: Erim Gurlemis
founders.background_notes: YC page says pharma consulting for oncology research, then Morgan Stanley wealth management AI implementation.

competitors.name: Machina Labs
competitors.what: AI-driven robotic manufacturing for defense parts
competitors.traction_then: Air Force Research Laboratory contract (Sept 2025) and a Lockheed Martin JASSM parts qualification contract
competitors.funding_then: Lockheed Martin Ventures holds a stake

competitors.name: Hadrian
competitors.what: Automated factories for defense and aerospace parts using its own AI model
competitors.traction_then: described as impressing the defense sector

competitors.name: X-Bow Systems
competitors.what: Rocket motor maker, first to deploy Lockheed Martin's Astris AI Factory

technical_complexity.rationale: Software to source, quote and schedule parts across suppliers is standard engineering for a two person team, but winning defense contracts and meeting quality and compliance rules is hard.

defensibility.rationale: Prime status and contract relationships could be sticky, but at founding the company has no reported contracts and funded rivals already hold government work.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent action against GUILD found; well funded defense manufacturing startups hold similar wedges.

market_need_then: Defense budgets and attention to supply chain bottlenecks were rising in 2025 and 2026, and YC's Summer 2026 batch was described as its largest defense tech cohort.

branding.domain_note: Uses guildai.co, not an exact .com; the name collides with Guild.ai, a separately funded AI agent startup.

identity.voice_and_tone: Direct, contract and delivery focused (win contracts, automate manufacturing, deliver to the government's door)

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand found; the common word Guild and the better funded Guild.ai and The Guild cause search confusion.

outcome_analysis: GUILD is an active Summer 2026 company with a team of two, so there is no outcome. It targets a hot defense manufacturing theme but starts without reported contracts or funding, against better funded manufacturers, and its name overlaps with other funded companies named Guild.
notes: No funding found for this company; funding results for Guild.ai (44M) and The Guild (20.5M Series A) are different companies. The company website fetch returned only navigation labels (Product, Team, Brand Style, Press, Funding) with no usable content. A third party directory describes the company as winning defense contracts, which is unconfirmed.
